rules.summary: Flag keydown event listeners on inputs or textareas intercepting Enter (event.key or event.code "Enter") to submit forms, send messages, or trigger actions without checking event.isComposing or event.keyCode === 229, breaking IME input in CJK languages.

keepWhen: Keydown event listeners on inputs or textareas checking event.key === "Enter" or event.code === "Enter" to trigger submission, search, or message sending without checking event.isComposing or event.keyCode === 229.
Custom enter-to-submit implementations intercepting Enter to call form.submit(), form.requestSubmit(), or trigger a click on a submit button without IME composition gating.
dropWhen: Keyup or keypress event listeners (composition has already ended by keyup).
Handlers that check event.isComposing or event.keyCode === 229.
Handlers that detect Enter only through event.keyCode === 13 or event.which === 13 (the keydown that confirms an IME composition reports keyCode 229, so these never fire mid-composition).
Handlers strictly requiring modifier keys (Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter) where IME character selection is not triggered.
Native form submit events or standard inputs inside a form with no custom Enter keydown listener (native Enter submission handles IME automatically).

Global document-level hotkeys, non-text UI widgets (buttons, menus, tabs, treeviews, dropdowns, modals, media players), or rich-text/code editor newline/indentation handlers rather than text-input submission.

findings.message: Keydown Enter listener triggers submission/action without checking event.isComposing or event.keyCode === 229 for IME composition safety

rules.summary: Replace shallow-copy array sorting, reversing, and reverse search with toSorted(), toReversed(), findLast(), and findLastIndex().

keepWhen: Array (or TypedArray via .slice()) copied via [...arr], arr.slice(), arr.slice(0), or arr.concat().
dropWhen: Spread [...x] on non-Array iterable (Set, Map, NodeList, HTMLCollection, DOMTokenList, FileList, arguments, string).
Sparse holes (slice preserves holes; toSorted fills undefined), callback index/array args for findLast/findLastIndex (does not apply to toReversed() or toSorted()), or un-inverted findIndex.

Visible project configuration in snippet targets pre-ES2023 (explicit engines.node < 20 or tsconfig lib/target older than ES2023; do not drop code merely because it uses var, ES5 syntax, or sits in a library/vendor file) or feature guards/polyfills.

findings.message: Use versions.toSorted((a,b)=> (b.version_id||b.version||0) - (a.version_id||a.version||0)) instead of copying before .sort().
Use atlasState.items.toSorted((a,b)=> hash01(a.id||a.chunk_id||a.node_id) - hash01(b.id||b.chunk_id||b.node_id)) instead of copying before .sort().

rules.summary: Replace standalone empty innerHTML assignments (el.innerHTML = "") with el.replaceChildren() to avoid HTML parsing and Trusted Types CSP failures.

keepWhen: A standalone statement clears a DOM Element, ShadowRoot, or SVGElement via .innerHTML = "" or .innerHTML = null (including when followed by appendChild/append calls to insert new nodes), where el.replaceChildren() avoids HTML parsing and Trusted Types CSP failures.
dropWhen: The receiver is a <template> element (where template.innerHTML = "" clears template.content, whereas template.replaceChildren() leaves template.content untouched) or a DocumentFragment / template.content (DocumentFragment has no innerHTML setter, so .innerHTML = "" is a no-op whereas replaceChildren() removes children).
The receiver is bare document or a non-DOM mock, serializer, virtual DOM node, or plain JavaScript object that happens to define an innerHTML property.

The empty innerHTML assignment is redundantly followed by another innerHTML assignment (= or +=) on the same receiver in the same block without intervening control flow, await/yield, or reads of its HTML/text content.

The assignment is part of a chained assignment or expression context whose empty-string result is consumed, relies on Custom Element disconnectedCallback() ordering, or sits inside a genuine legacy-browser DOM polyfill/shim or explicit replaceChildren() feature-detection guard.

findings.message: Assigning empty innerHTML invokes the HTML parser and fails under Trusted Types; use element.replaceChildren() (or element.replaceChildren(newContent)) instead.
